title: session.finished
description: The session reached the end of its life. Parity with flowpilot's terminal status + the usage totals of agent_sessions.

status.description: How it ended. The four beyond completed/failed exist so that a healthy outcome (quota_paused), an invalid ref (resume_failed) and a stop of our own (timed_out) are never read as a bug to investigate. The two stops of our own — wall-clock and silence — both end up in timed_out, and what separates them is timeout_reason; stuck has no relation to silence, it is the slot for whoever has no slot (pending/running/cancelled).

exit_code.description: The exit code of the engine's process, when there was a process with an exit.

timeout_reason.description: Which watchdog stopped the session, when the one that stopped it was the adapter. wall_clock = it blew the wall clock; silence = it went the whole budget without producing output. null when it does not apply, or when the adapter reported no cause — never filled in by guesswork. The values are vocabulary of the EngineAdapter interface, which is what produces them.

usage.description: Token totals frozen at the end of life. null when the engine reported nothing — never collapse into zero. No cost field: cost is engine vocabulary.

failure_kind.description: What KIND of failure this was, when the status alone does not say (t265, t296). The same move as timeout_reason, applied to the other ambiguous status: a crash, an engine that REFUSED to answer and an account that answered 429 all end up in failed, and the three deserve different answers — a crash is worth retrying now, a refusal reproduces identically on every retry (measured in t198: the same prompt refused four times in a row before the fifth session worked), and a quota heals itself at a known instant (measured in t296: three attempts in twenty seconds, US$9.3, and a job flagged 'consecutive failures' for an account that was merely at its limit). A closed set because the word is OURS: a second value entered when a second kind of failure was measured, never because an engine invented one. null/absent when the adapter reported no kind at all — never deduced from the exit code, which is precisely what all three have in common.

refusal_category.description: How the engine itself classified the refusal, when it classified it (t265). The ENGINE's word, verbatim and untranslated — reasoning_extraction is what t198's bisection read from the real frame. An open set of values on purpose, like models' and unlike failure_kind's beside it: the category is engine vocabulary, and a closed enum would demand a schema change for every new category. null when the engine refused and said nothing more, which is a real shape of the frame and not a defect.

models.description: Which models ran the session, as the engine named them. A list because a session runs more than one — measured against the real CLI, a single turn returned two — and collapsing into 'the' model would attribute the whole bill to the wrong one. null when the engine named none; an empty list is not an answer, null is what says 'nothing'. An open set of values on purpose: the identifier is the engine's, and a closed enum would demand a schema change for every new model.

output.description: The STRUCTURED result the session reported from the node (t253) — what the next node's input projection reads. With no nested required and no declared properties, on purpose: the shape inside is the one the output schema of the skill pinned by the node declares (D9), and freezing it here would demand one event schema per problem class. null when nothing structured was reported — the same reading as usage and models beside it: an absence is an absence and never an empty object.

output_accepted.description: Whether the session's report was ACCEPTED (t268). The same fact as output_schema_error above, seen from the side of whoever has to act: the list says why a report was refused and exists only when there was a refusal; this one says whether it was accepted, and is recorded on every closing — true when nothing was reported and when the report matched the output schema of the pinned skill, false only when that schema refused it. A boolean and not a derivation of the list beside it because the one that reads it is the runner, in the response of PATCH /finish itself, to decide whether the job may move: there 'no reasons' and 'not checked' would be the same absence, and the difference between the two is a job that travels an edge chosen from a report that was never recorded.

output_schema_error.description: Why the reported output did not match the skill's schema (t253). Present only when there was a divergence, and then output goes to null: the session's terminal status is recorded either way, because losing the end of the session over a malformed self-report would be strictly worse — a work node's self-report was never evidence (a gate verifies with evidence of its own). The whole list, never just the first reason, for the same reason the envelope validation returns them all.
